canDo.de: Ich kann aus der Vergangenheit auf Späteres blicken: Pläne (was going to), unmittelbar Bevorstehendes (was about to), spätere Folgen (would) und Vorgesehenes (was to).
canDo.en: I can look from the past at what came later: plans (was going to), what was imminent (was about to), later results (would) and what was meant to be (was to).

de: Ging es um einen Plan von damals? Nimm was going to.
Stand es kurz bevor, dann kam etwas dazwischen? Nimm was about to + when.
Blickst du erzählend auf Späteres? Nimm would. War es vorgesehen? Nimm was to.
en: Was it a plan from back then? Use was going to.
Was it just about to happen, then something intervened? Use was about to + when.
Do you look ahead while telling a story? Use would. Was it meant to be? Use was to.

name.de: was going to · der Plan von damals
name.en: was going to · the plan back then

form.en: was / were going to + base form

use.de: Mit was going to nennst du einen Plan aus der Vergangenheit. Oft kam es anders: „We were going to launch in May, but the supplier was late.“
use.en: With was going to you name a plan from the past. Often it turned out differently: “We were going to launch in May, but the supplier was late.”

ex.en: We were going to launch in May, but the supplier was late.
ex.de: Wir wollten im Mai starten, aber der Lieferant war spät dran.

ex.en: I was going to call you, but the line was busy.
ex.de: Ich wollte dich anrufen, aber die Leitung war besetzt.

ex.en: She said she was going to resign.

trap.bad: We are going to launch in May, but the supplier was late.
trap.good: We were going to launch in May, but the supplier was late.

cause.de: Ein Plan aus der Vergangenheit braucht was oder were going to. Das Hilfsverb are gehört in die Gegenwart.
cause.en: A plan from the past needs was or were going to. The auxiliary are belongs to the present.

diff.de: Was going to nennt einen Plan. Was about to heißt: kurz davor, es jetzt zu tun.
diff.en: Was going to names a plan. Was about to means: on the point of doing it now.

ccq.s: We were going to launch in May.

q.de: Hat der Start vielleicht nicht geklappt?
q.en: Did the launch perhaps not work out?

nudge.de: Geht es um einen Plan von damals? Dann passt was going to.
nudge.en: Is it about a plan from back then? Then was going to fits.

name.de: was about to · gerade im Begriff
name.en: was about to · on the point of

form.de: was / were about to + Grundform (… when …)
form.en: was / were about to + base form (… when …)

use.de: Was about to heißt: Die Handlung stand unmittelbar bevor, dann kam etwas dazwischen. Oft folgt ein when-Satz: „I was about to leave when the client called.“
use.en: Was about to means: the action was just about to happen, then something intervened. A when-clause often follows: “I was about to leave when the client called.”

ex.en: I was about to leave when the client called.
ex.de: Ich wollte gerade gehen, als der Kunde anrief.

ex.en: We were about to sign when the lawyer found an error.
ex.de: Wir wollten gerade unterschreiben, als der Anwalt einen Fehler fand.

ex.en: The meeting was about to start when the power failed.
ex.de: Die Besprechung sollte gerade beginnen, als der Strom ausfiel.

trap.bad: I was about leaving when the client called.
trap.good: I was about to leave when the client called.

cause.de: Das deutsche „gerade am Gehen“ führt zu „about leaving“. Englisch sagt about to und die Grundform.
cause.en: The German “gerade am Gehen” leads to “about leaving”. English says about to and the base form.

diff.de: Was about to heißt: kurz davor. Was going to nennt einen Plan.
diff.en: Was about to means: just before. Was going to names a plan.

ccq.s: I was about to leave when she called.

q.de: War ich noch da, als sie anrief?
q.en: Was I still there when she called?

nudge.de: Stand die Handlung kurz bevor? Dann passt was about to, oft mit when.
nudge.en: Was the action just about to happen? Then was about to fits, often with when.

use.de: Beim Erzählen blickst du von einem Punkt der Vergangenheit auf Späteres: „She joined in 2015 and would later lead the office.“ Auch nach Verben wie promised steht would statt will.
use.en: When telling a story you look from a point in the past at something later: “She joined in 2015 and would later lead the office.” After verbs like promised too, would replaces will.

ex.en: She joined the firm in 2015 and would later lead the Berlin office.
ex.de: Sie kam 2015 zur Firma und leitete später das Berliner Büro.

ex.en: He promised that he would send the report by Monday.
ex.de: Er versprach, den Bericht bis Montag zu schicken.

ex.en: The product would go on to win several awards.
ex.de: Das Produkt gewann später mehrere Preise.

trap.bad: In 2015 she joined the firm and will later lead the Berlin office.
trap.good: In 2015 she joined the firm and would later lead the Berlin office.

cause.de: Wer aus der Vergangenheit auf Späteres blickt, braucht would. Will gehört in die Gegenwart.
cause.en: If you look from the past at something later, you need would. Will belongs to the present.

contrast.a: She would later lead the office.
contrast.b: She was to lead the office.

diff.de: Would zeigt nur, dass es später geschah. Was to sagt, dass es so vorgesehen war.
diff.en: Would shows only that it happened later. Was to says it was meant to be.

ccq.s: She would later lead the office.

nudge.de: Blickst du aus der Vergangenheit auf Späteres? Dann passt would, nicht will.
nudge.en: Do you look from the past at something later? Then would fits, not will.

form.de: was / were to + Grundform · was / were to have + 3. Form
form.en: was / were to + base form · was / were to have + participle

use.de: Was to nennt, was vorgesehen war oder bestimmt schien: „The new office was to open in June.“ Mit was to have + 3. Form sagst du, dass es nicht geschah. Im Alltag sagt man meist was supposed to, was to klingt förmlich.
use.en: Was to names what was planned or seemed destined: “The new office was to open in June.” With was to have + participle you say it did not happen. In everyday speech people mostly say was supposed to, was to sounds formal.

ex.en: The new office was to open in June, but the permit was delayed.
ex.de: Das neue Büro sollte im Juni eröffnen, aber die Genehmigung verzögerte sich.

ex.en: She was to become the youngest director in the firm.
ex.de: Sie sollte die jüngste Direktorin der Firma werden.

ex.en: The talks were to have ended on Friday.
ex.de: Die Gespräche hätten am Freitag enden sollen.

trap.bad: The new office should open in June, but the permit was delayed.
trap.good: The new office was to open in June, but the permit was delayed.

cause.de: Das deutsche „sollte“ wird hier nicht zu should. Für einen Plan in der Vergangenheit gilt was to.
cause.en: The German “sollte” does not become should here. For a plan in the past was to is used.

contrast.a: She was to lead the office.
contrast.b: She would later lead the office.

diff.de: Was to sagt, dass es vorgesehen war. Would zeigt nur, dass es später geschah.
diff.en: Was to says it was meant to be. Would shows only that it happened later.

ccq.s: The talks were to end on Friday.

q.de: Nennt der Satz, was geplant war?
q.en: Does the sentence name what was planned?

nudge.de: Geht es um etwas Vorgesehenes? Dann passt was to, bei einem nicht erfüllten Plan was to have + 3. Form.
nudge.en: Is it about something meant to happen? Then was to fits, for an unfulfilled plan was to have + participle.
